newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut banks freed from mandatory t-bill buying.
newsitem.headline: Beirut banks freed from mandatory t-bill buying.

text.p: Lebanon's central bank on Wednesday exempted commercial banks from compulsory subscription of 40 percent of their Lebanese pound deposits in treasury bills.
The Bank of Lebanon said in a statement that the decision was announced after the weekly meeting of the Bank's Central Council grouping Governor Riad Salameh and his four deputies.

"Governor Riad Salameh announced after the meeting that the Council has decided to exempt commercial banks from compulsory subscription of 40 percent of their pound deposits in treasury bills...The decision means that any bank is no longer bound to invest in regular bills," the Bank said.

According to the latest figures from the Lebanese Banks Association grouping 79 of Lebanon's 81 commercial banks, the banks' total Lebanese pound deposits stood at 13,636 billion Lebanese pounds at the end of 1996.
"The Central Council reached this conviction following the relief felt by the Bank of Lebanon over the monetary situation and the treasury accounts' solvency," the bank statement added.
Salameh said the decision would have a positive impact on the economy "because it frees important funds that the public or private sector can benefit from," it added.
($1 = 1,552 Lebanese pounds at the end of 1996)
